properties.address: 1540 Maine Ave SW, Washington, DC 20004, USA

properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation seated on Atlantic Coastal Plain alluvial silt and gravel over dense Piedmont crystalline metamorphic bedrock (Sykesville Formation gneiss and schist). Primary monument lithics comprise Cockeysville white marble ashlar at the lower 46-meter tier, transitioning cleanly to Massachusetts and Maine white marble ashlar on upper courses, backed by coursed granite rubble and bluestone gneiss. Surrounding background architecture features Bedford Indiana oolitic limestone, coarse-grained granite plinths, and structural terracotta tile underlayment.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Surrounding parkland and boulevards populated by mature *Ulmus americana* (American elm), *Quercus phellos* (willow oak), *Quercus alba* (white oak), and *Platanus occidentalis* (American sycamore). Early September phenology exhibits full, dense crown volumes with deep emerald to mature olive-green leaf pigmentation, displaying early late-summer canopy heaviness without active autumnal abscission.

properties.architectural_summary: Central monumental obelisk standing at 169.3 meters, displaying precise 10:1 height-to-base taper terminating in a 16.8-meter pyramidal apex (pyramidion). Plumb vertical masonry courses with rectified planar geometry. Base surrounded by a concentric paved circular plaza with fifty radial flagpole stanchions and a low-profile cuboid security pavilion at the east portal. Midground features the National Museum of African American History and Culture exhibiting a three-tiered inverted trapezoidal corona (ziggurat massing). Federal Triangle urban perimeter comprises Classical Revival and Beaux-Arts federal administrative complexes with rusticated ground stories, monumental Doric/Ionic colonnades, entablatures, and pitched hipped roofs.
